REPRODUCIBLE BY DESIGN

What the model can see.

Temporal evaluation, historical features, and a clear boundary between a demonstration and external validation.

Data & provenance

This release uses an original seeded transaction simulator. It includes ordinary payments, benign payment hubs and payroll alongside injected suspicious patterns. Labels describe the simulator's planted patterns, not real investigations.

IBM AML-Data is the planned external benchmark. It is also synthetic, with separate CDLA-Sharing-1.0 data terms. Its data has not been downloaded or evaluated in this release.

Official IBM dataset source

Chronological protocol

Training precedes validation, and validation precedes the untouched evaluation window. Preprocessing is fitted on training data. Model settings are fixed in advance; validation is reported separately. Test labels never enter model features.

All transactions at the same timestamp are scored before that timestamp's history is updated. Future transactions cannot change earlier feature values.

Models & features

Logistic Regression and Random Forest are trained classifiers. Isolation Forest is an unsupervised anomaly baseline in the offline comparison. A high-amount rule provides a simple reference.

The ablation compares current-transaction features against current fields plus strictly historical account features. Account identifiers index history but are not model inputs.

    Training & deployment

    Python, NumPy, pandas and scikit-learn run the offline experiments. Native JavaScript performs local inference with exported model weights and trees. Python/JavaScript parity tests verify the deployment contract.

    No database or inference API is needed. Input files and edited scenarios remain in browser memory. Refreshing the page clears them.

    MEASURED EXPERIMENTS

    Compare evidence, not accuracy alone.

    These results come from executed experiments on the original simulator. They do not establish real-bank effectiveness.

    Held-out model comparison

    Model / feature setAPROC-AUCPrecision@5%Recall@5%

    Average Precision (AP) summarizes the precision–recall curve. It is not interchangeable with trapezoidal PR-AUC. Rankings use a fixed 5% alert budget.

    Average Precision

    The positive prevalence is the reference for random ranking.

    Experiment manifest

    Shared accounts across windows represent existing-account scoring. This release does not demonstrate generalization to unseen institutions, countries or banking customers. Repeated-seed intervals and an external benchmark remain follow-up research.

    ARASH AMINI · AI / DATA SCIENCE PORTFOLIO

    Temporal anomaly detection, made inspectable.

    A research prototype connecting transaction analysis, machine learning and a usable interactive interface.

    Research question

    At a fixed review budget, do strictly historical account features improve detection of planted suspicious transactions compared with transaction-only features?

    What this project demonstrates

    • Reproducible data generation, feature engineering and model training.
    • Chronological evaluation and tabular-versus-history ablations.
    • Export of actual trained models with verified local inference.
    • Interactive network inspection and transaction perturbations.
    • Independent review of leakage, provenance and input handling.
    View repository

    Release boundaries

    This is a simulation research prototype. A model score is not evidence of criminal activity and is not a calibrated probability. The system is not a production AML or compliance service.

    The interface uses English so academic reviewers can inspect the project. Reports to the project owner are provided in Persian.

    Development & contribution

    Arash Amini initiated and owns this project. Implementation and review were assisted by AI agents. Prepared source documents the architecture, experiment commands, test evidence and limitations. Source is available through the GitHub repository.
